note.question: What role does targeted couponing play in online auctions?
note.overview: To study the role of targeted couponing in auctions, we develop a stylized model in which bidders have heterogeneous valuations and participation costs wherein their entry probabilities are endogenous. Couponing impacts the seller’s profit in two ways: (i) impact on bidders’ entry probability including negative externalities for the bidder who does not receive a coupon and (ii) value extraction. The paper finds that targeting a coupon to the low-valuation bidder can be optimal for the firm even if it leads to a reduction in the joint entry probability of the two bidders because of the benefit from value extraction.

To study the role of targeted couponing in auctions, we develop a stylized model in which bidders have heterogeneous valuations and participation costs wherein their entry probabilities are endogenous.
This is consistent with the literature, including Narasimhan (1982, 1984) models of consumers with higher wage rates as facing higher opportunity cost of time.

conditions: we assume that the cost of the good to the seller is sunk, and therefore, the seller’s objective is to maximize revenue from the auction (Myerson 1981).
We consider a private-value auction where each bidder knows his valuation for the item, which is independent of others’ valuations.

The private-value setting has been supported by extensive literature that has empirically studied online auction platforms like eBay (Hou and Rego 2007, Ockenfels and Roth 2006, Roth and Ockenfels 2002, Zeithammer 2006).
